Byggettan agreed to pay fees for monitoring the wages of workers. But the workers did not want to pay the fees because they did not think the work was of use to them. The case was taken to the Labour Court, which ruled in favour of the workers. The court ruled that the Union was not obliged to levy the fees in question. It said that the deductions were tantamount to forced union membership or, at least, involved an unacceptable compulsion to join the Union or another trade union.
